Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Washout and re-stimulation (priming) test
ideas.description: Pulse cells with a defined AP-1 stimulus (e.g., TPA or EGF), wash out, and wait through a quiescent interval. Then re-stimulate and compare naive and primed cells by time-resolved RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. Memory is supported if primed cells show faster or stronger induction of AP-1 target genes, and that advantage disappears when the interval is extended or the washout is reversed. The 'undo' step is the control: a true memory should persist after the stimulus is removed.

ideas.title: Acute degradation of c-Jun or c-Fos during the quiescent interval
ideas.description: Tag endogenous c-Jun or c-Fos with a degron (e.g., dTAG or AID) and degrade it after priming but before re-stimulation. If the primed response survives loss of the AP-1 protein, the memory is stored in chromatin or other marks rather than in the transcription factor itself. If the advantage is lost, AP-1 must be continuously present to maintain the memory.

ideas.title: Heritable lineage recording of AP-1 activity history
ideas.description: Drive a stable reporter (Cre-loxP switch, or a CRISPR-based cumulative recorder) from AP-1-responsive enhancers so that each past AP-1 activation leaves a permanent, heritable mark. This works like madder staining bone, recording past exposure in the tissue itself. Sorting or imaging cells by mark, then tracking their clonal descendants, tests whether prior AP-1 activity is inherited through divisions and predicts later responses.

ideas.title: Motif-level mutagenesis of memory-associated enhancers
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base editing or prime editing to mutate the AP-1 motifs in candidate enhancers one at a time, leaving other elements and baseline transcription intact. Then test whether each mutation removes the priming-dependent gain in re-induction without affecting the first response. This separates the role of AP-1 binding in memory from its role in the initial activation, and it works like a primer's cue that is needed only for later recall.

ideas.title: Chromatin bookmark persistence with CUT&RUN and epigenetic inhibition
ideas.description: Map AP-1 (Fos/Jun family) occupancy and H3K27ac, H3K4me1, and Pol II pausing by CUT&RUN and ChIP-seq at multiple time points after priming, including the quiescent phase. Then inhibit p300/CBP or BRD4 during the interval to test whether retained enhancer marks at those sites are required for faster re-induction. If the memory depends on these marks, blocking their maintenance should erase the primed response while leaving the first response intact.
